What you will learn

  • Build a calculator, personal page, log utility, Git workflow and device automation.
  • Check meaningful outcomes rather than unconditional PASS messages.

Before you begin

Each project names its prerequisites. Work in disposable projects, export first and keep credentials out of code. Test each project on your phone and compare expected and actual results.

P1 · A C calculator

Brief: menu-driven arithmetic on small finite numbers. Needs: Chapters 2/8/15 and Terminal input. Plan: isolate compute, validate the operation, check scanf, refuse division by zero, loop until q. This is a teaching calculator, not a hardened arbitrary-precision service.

calc.c

#include <stdio.h>
int compute(double a, char op, double b, double *out) {
    switch (op) {
        case '+': *out = a + b; return 1;
        case '-': *out = a - b; return 1;
        case '*': *out = a * b; return 1;
        case '/': if (b == 0.0) return 0; *out = a / b; return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}
int main(void) {
    char op;
    double a, b, result;
    while (1) {
        puts("Operation (+ - * /), q quit:");
        if (scanf(" %c", &op) != 1) return 1;
        if (op == 'q') break;
        if (op != '+' && op != '-' && op != '*' && op != '/') {
            puts("Choose a listed operation");
            continue;
        }
        puts("Two numbers:");
        if (scanf("%lf %lf", &a, &b) != 2) return 1;
        if (compute(a, op, b, &result)) printf("Result: %.2f\n", result);
        else puts("Cannot divide by zero");
    }
    return 0;
}

Build and run P1

cc calc.c -o calc
./calc

Result: choose + then 2 3 → Result:5.00; choose * then 4 5 →20.00; choose / then 4 0 → Cannot divide by zero; q exits. Record actual prompts/output on the phone. You can reuse Chapter 15’s Makefile pattern with calc.c and calc as the target.

Stretch: keep the last five successful results in a fixed array. Test wraparound without writing past its bounds.

P2 · Your personal page

Brief: a small page about you, with local data and a click counter. Needs: Chapters 6/12/14, no Linux download. Plan: keep HTML, CSS, JS and JSON separate; fetch only the sibling data file; handle a failure visibly. Use a fictional name while testing LAN exposure.

index.html

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My phone-made page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  <script src="app.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body>
  <h1 id="name">My page</h1>
  <p id="bio">Loading local data…</p>
  <button id="count" type="button">Clicks: 0</button>
</body>
</html>

style.css

:root { --accent: #3ddc84; }
body { margin: 2rem auto; padding: 1rem; max-width: 40rem;
       background: #101713; color: #edf2ed; font-family: sans-serif; }
h1 { color: var(--accent); }
button { padding: 1rem; font: inherit; }
button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent); }

app.js

fetch("data.json")
  .then(response => {
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error("HTTP " + response.status);
    return response.json();
  })
  .then(data => {
    document.querySelector("#name").textContent = data.name;
    document.querySelector("#bio").textContent = data.bio;
  })
  .catch(error => {
    document.querySelector("#bio").textContent = "Could not load data";
    console.error(error);
  });
let clicks = 0;
document.querySelector("#count").addEventListener("click", event => {
  clicks += 1;
  event.currentTarget.textContent = "Clicks: " + clicks;
});

data.json

{"name":"CodeC learner","bio":"I make small things on my phone."}

Result: RUN index.html → CodeC learner and the bio; button increments after each tap. Change data.json, save and compare. Export the whole project ZIP. LAN sharing is optional and only for non-sensitive files.

Stretch: add a second HTML page with a relative link back. Preserve keyboard focus and readable contrast.

P3 · A log summarizer

Brief: count lines/words/characters and print the top three whitespace-separated words. Needs: Python3 from Chapter 10. Plan: read a UTF-8 file, normalize case, count with a dictionary, sort by count then name. Punctuation stays part of a word in this deliberately simple version.

summarize.py

import sys
from pathlib import Path

if len(sys.argv) != 2:
    print("Usage: python3 summarize.py FILE", file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(2)
try:
    text = Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
except (OSError, UnicodeError) as error:
    print("Cannot read:", error, file=sys.stderr)
    raise SystemExit(1)
words = text.lower().split()
counts = {}
for word in words:
    counts[word] = counts.get(word, 0) + 1
print("lines:", len(text.splitlines()))
print("words:", len(words))
print("chars:", len(text))
for word, count in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))[:3]:
    print(word, count)

Create a disposable fixture and summarize it

printf 'red blue red\ngreen blue red\n' > sample.log
python3 summarize.py sample.log

Expected summary

lines: 2
words: 6
chars: 28
red 3
blue 2
green 1

Result: compare this fixture, then two of your own non-sensitive text files. Stretch: add a --json mode using the standard json module, preserving the error exit codes.

P4 · A Git-backed project

Brief: keep the calculator source under version control in your own repository. Needs: Chapter 11, Git and your own account/repository. Plan: create a private test repository on GitHub, clone it in Projects, add calc.c, review/stage source, commit and push. Do not commit the calc binary.

  1. Create the repository on GitHub and initialize a README. Clone its HTTPS URL in CodeC. Supply credentials through the panel’s Git Credentials dialog if needed.
  2. Copy your reviewed calc.c into that project. Commit only source and the README. Push, inspect the remote/branch result, then verify the files on GitHub.
  3. With clean work, use New branch for a practice branch. Edit the README, commit and push that branch.
  4. Merge using a reviewed GitHub pull request on your own repository, then return to the original branch and pull. Inspect a conflict before resolving it; do not force-push as a shortcut.

Result: GitHub shows the changed source on the intended branch, not merely an app toast. A failed push remains local and retryable. Stretch: add the exact build/run command to README so another person can reproduce your result.

P5 · A morning automation

Brief: optionally update packages, read the battery and request a spoken greeting. Needs: Chapters 5/9/13, Bash/sed and foreground CodeC Terminal, working TextToSpeech. Plan: make every failure visible; parse percentage, reject absent/out-of-range values and require explicit consent before package mutation.

morning.sh

if test "${1:-}" = "--upgrade"; then
    printf 'This updates installed packages. Continue? Type YES: '
    read -r answer
    if test "$answer" != "YES"; then
        printf 'FAIL: upgrade not approved\n' >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    if pkg update && pkg upgrade -y; then
        printf 'PASS: packages updated\n'
    else
        printf 'FAIL: package update\n' >&2
        exit 1
    fi
else
    printf 'SKIP: package updates (use --upgrade to request them)\n'
fi
json=$(codec-battery) || { printf 'FAIL: battery query\n' >&2; exit 1; }
level=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | sed -n 's/.*"percentage":\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p')
case "$level" in ''|*[!0-9]*) printf 'FAIL: battery value\n' >&2; exit 1;; esac
if test "$level" -gt 100; then
    printf 'FAIL: battery range\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi
printf 'Battery: %s%%\n' "$level"
if codec-tts "Good morning, battery at $level percent"; then
    printf 'PASS: speech request accepted\n'
else
    printf 'FAIL: speech request\n' >&2
    exit 1
fi

Run without package mutation

bash morning.sh

Result: SKIP for package updates, current battery percentage, then accepted speech or an honest FAIL. A successful API return is not proof that you heard sound: record both separately. To exercise the upgrade step on a backed-up environment, run bash morning.sh --upgrade, read the prompt and type YES only if you intend pkg update and pkg upgrade -y. Network/permission/voice failures must not be relabelled PASS.

Check on your phone: capture the actual battery JSON, command result and whether speech was audible. Record whether you explicitly tested the optional upgrade path or left it skipped. Host syntax/stub checks cannot replace this transcript.

Stretch: append a timestamped result to morning.log using >> without hiding stderr. Do not schedule unattended package changes or silent sharing.

Five verbs you can reuse

Compile, script, automate, version and preview. Keep projects small enough to inspect and document the prerequisites needed on a fresh phone. When something fails, the next chapter gives a diagnostic ladder; the two final chapters then cover optional AI without surrendering review.

Try it yourself

  1. Complete P1’s +, *, zero-division and quit checks on the device and record expected versus actual.
  2. Run P5 deliberately, record real outcomes and keep package upgrades opt-in. A browser test cannot confirm phone permissions or audible speech.
  3. Export the web project and run the Python summary on two harmless files; verify the intended Git remote before sharing any work.

Common mistakes

  • Project dependencies are real; an uninstalled runtime is not fixed by syntax highlighting.
  • Use Terminal for interactive C and avoid committing generated binaries.
  • Speech “accepted” and speech “heard” are separate observations.
  • A project that only works because of an undocumented phone setup is not reproducible yet.
